Case Study Overview

T Expo — The App

Role: UI/UX Designer
Platform: Mobile (iOS & Android)
Tool: Figma
Category: Travel & Tourism

What is T Expo?

T Expo is a community-powered travel discovery app designed for tourists exploring destinations across India. The app combines curated place listings with real-time community updates — giving every traveler access to live on-ground information before and during their visit.

The design focuses on three core user journeys: Discovery (finding places by category), Verification (checking live status and crowd levels), and Contribution (posting updates for the community).

With a clean, light mobile interface using soft teal and green accents, T Expo bridges the gap between travel planning and real-world conditions.

Challenge & Solution

Why T Expo exists

Every traveler has faced the frustration of outdated information. T Expo was born to solve this real pain.

❌

Problem Statement

  • Tourists arrive at destinations only to find them unexpectedly closed, overcrowded, or inaccessible due to weather or local events.
  • Existing travel apps show static, outdated information — no real-time crowd levels or live weather conditions at the spot.
  • Travelers cannot easily discover nearby places by category (temples, waterfalls, adventure spots) from a single interface.
  • There is no community-driven platform where fellow tourists can share on-ground updates, photos, and status reports.
  • Trip planning suffers from information overload but a lack of verified, current, location-specific data.
✅

How T Expo Solves It

  • Live Status panel on every destination page shows whether a place is currently Open, Closed, or Crowded — updated in real time by the community.
  • Crowd Level indicator gives a visual bar so visitors can gauge how busy a place is before committing to the trip.
  • Category-based discovery (Food, Adventure, Swimming Spots, Photo Spots, Top Places) lets users filter destinations that match their interests.
  • Community Updates feed allows travelers to post photos and written updates directly from the location, helping future visitors plan better.
  • Horizontal type filters (Temples, Waterfalls, Rivers…) enable quick browsing by landmark category with visible counts.
Key Features

What makes T Expo powerful

Every feature was designed around one question: what does a traveler need to know right now?

🗺️

Smart Discovery

Filter destinations by type — Temples, Waterfalls, Rivers, and more. Category cards show item counts so users know what's available before browsing.

🔴 Live Status

Live Open/Close Status

Each destination shows a real-time Live Status — Open, Closed, or Crowded — so tourists never waste a journey to a shut gate.

👥

Crowd Level Indicator

A visual progress bar tells users how packed a destination currently is, helping them choose the best time to visit for a comfortable experience.

📸

Community Updates Feed

Travelers post real-time photos and situation reports from the spot. Updates include weather conditions, event notices, and access alerts.

➕

Post Your Update

Users can upload photos, set current status, and write a description to help fellow travelers. Simple 3-step form keeps contribution frictionless.

⭐

Top Places Curation

Editors curate the best destinations across India with ratings, making it easy for first-time visitors to find must-see spots at a glance.

Design Process

How I designed T Expo

A structured design thinking approach — from raw research to polished, user-tested screens.

01

Empathize — User Research

Conducted interviews and surveys with frequent domestic tourists in India. Identified key pain points: unreliable information, surprise closures, and inability to gauge crowd density before arriving. Created user personas representing solo travelers, family groups, and photography enthusiasts.

02

Define — Problem Framing

Synthesized research into a core problem statement: tourists lack access to live, trustworthy, on-the-ground information about destinations. Defined success metrics around reducing "wasted trips" and increasing traveler confidence in planning decisions.

03

Ideate — Concept Exploration

Explored multiple concepts — from pure map-based interfaces to social-media-style feeds. Settled on a hybrid model: curated listings (for discovery) + community updates (for live information). Sketched wireframes for the three core screens: Home, Detail, and Add Update.

04

Prototype — High-Fidelity Design

Built high-fidelity screens in Figma with a consistent design system — light teal/green color palette, rounded card components, live status indicators, and iconographic category chips. Applied a clean, approachable aesthetic that works for all age groups.

05

Test — Validation & Iteration

Shared prototypes with target users for feedback sessions. Key insight: users wanted the crowd level bar to be more visually prominent and the "Post Update" button to be always accessible. Iterated to add the floating action button and improved the status toggle interaction in the Add Update screen.

Screen Walkthrough

Every screen, explained

A deep-dive into each screen — what it does, why it was designed this way, and how it solves a real traveler problem.

Screen 01 — Home

Discovery starts here

The home screen is the front door of T Expo. It opens with the T expo logo, a prominent search bar, and horizontal category pills — All, Temples, Waterfalls, River — letting users instantly filter by place type.

Below the filters, icon-based category cards (Top Places ⭐, Food 250, Adventure 140, Swimming Spot 100, Photo Spot 250) give a visual count of available destinations in each category — setting clear expectations before the user dives in.

Place cards follow — each showing a hero photo, destination name, star rating, a weather icon, and a live Open status badge. Users can scan multiple destinations at a glance and decide instantly.

Category Filters Live Status Badge Star Ratings Weather Icon
Screen 02 — Place Detail

Live info before you go

Tapping a destination opens the detail page — topped by a full-bleed hero photo. Below it sits the full address with a pin icon, so users can navigate directly from the app.

The Live Status card is the heart of this screen. It shows a green "Open" dot, a timestamp ("Updated 5 min ago"), and a Crowd Level bar — a green progress indicator showing real-time busyness so tourists can decide whether to visit now or come back later.

Three tabs — Updates, Info, Photos — organise the content. The Updates tab (active) shows community posts like "Weather is Rain" from user Adharsh, posted 1 min ago, with a real photo, likes, comments, and share buttons. A floating ＋ button invites users to post their own update.

Live Status Crowd Level Bar Community Feed Tab Navigation
Screen 03 — Add Update

Give back to the community

This screen turns every traveler into a contributor. Titled "Add Update", it's a simple 3-step form designed to lower the barrier of sharing — because useful data only exists if people post it.

Add Photo (optional) — a large tap-to-upload zone with a camera icon encourages users to attach a real photo from the spot. Making it optional removes friction for quick updates.

Current Status — three pill buttons: Open (blue, active), Close, Crowded. One tap sets the status without typing anything. This data feeds directly into the Live Status on the detail page.

Your Update — a large text area with placeholder "Describe the current situation…" A reminder at the bottom reads "Your update will help other travelers plan their visit" — reinforcing the purpose. The blue "Post Update" button closes the flow.

Photo Upload Status Toggle Text Input Post CTA

The Designer

About Me

I'm Adharsh AV, UI/UX Designer.

I design digital experiences that are intuitive, beautiful, and grounded in real human needs. My process starts with deep empathy for the user and ends only when every interaction feels effortless.

T Expo is a personal project born from my own frustration as a traveler — arriving at places without the information I needed. I designed it to be the app I wished existed: live, community-powered, and genuinely useful on the ground.

I believe great UI/UX is invisible. Users shouldn't notice the design — they should simply feel that everything just works.
